title: Change sets, Metadata API deployment, unlocked packages, and managed packages
objectives: Describe change sets as an org-to-org metadata channel between related organizations, not a Git package.
Describe Metadata API deployment (including CLI wrapping it) as moving customization XML, not business records.
Choose unlocked packages for most internal apps because version control is the metadata source of truth.
Choose managed 2GP when distributing on AppExchange, and state that 1GP cannot currently be migrated to 2GP.
diagnostic_question: You must promote LAB_ metadata to three orgs, delete nothing yet, and maybe list an app on AppExchange later. Do you use a change set, a source deploy, an unlocked package, or a managed package—and what evidence would change your mind?
definition: A package is a container you fill with metadata. Change sets move selected metadata components between related orgs. Metadata API deploy/retrieve (and CLI project deploy) move customization files. Unlocked packages are the usual internal, source-driven package type unless you plan to distribute on AppExchange, in which case use second-generation managed packaging. You cannot currently migrate a first-generation managed package to 2GP. ([Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm); [Second-Generation Managed Packaging](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg2_dev.meta/pkg2_dev/sfdx_dev_dev2gp.htm); [Understanding Metadata API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_api_intro.htm))
why_it_matters: Picking change sets when you needed Git-versioned unlocked packages, or unlocked packages when you needed AppExchange managed 2GP, is a classic interview fail. Coverage is not universal: Metadata Coverage is the channel truth.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of shipping. A change set is a pallet that only moves between two docks already in the same port family. Metadata API deployment is the container crane that loads XML onto any ship you can authorize. An unlocked package is a labeled container you can restock and subscribers can still edit. A managed package is a sealed commercial crate with namespace locks for AppExchange. Git is the bill of lading for source-driven packages. None of these cranes load passenger cargo (business data).
deeper_explanation: Unlocked packages are especially suited for internal business apps. Unless you plan to distribute on AppExchange, unlocked is the right package type for most use cases: organize existing metadata, package an app, extend an AppExchange app, or package new metadata. They follow source-driven development: the source of truth of the metadata in the package is version control, not the org. ([Unlocked Packages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_unlocked_pkg_intro.htm))

Managed 2GP is for AppExchange partners to develop, distribute, and manage apps. Version control is truth; there are no packaging or patch orgs in that 2GP model. You cannot currently migrate 1GP to 2GP. If you are a customer or SI not distributing to multiple customers, unlocked packaging is preferred. ([2GP](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.pkg2_dev.meta/pkg2_dev/sfdx_dev_dev2gp.htm))

Metadata API moves metadata between orgs; it does not work directly with business data. CLI project deploy is the usual modern client. Change sets also move metadata between connected related orgs (for example sandbox to production) and rely on Metadata API under the hood, but they are not a Git package and they do not replace coverage checks. ([Understanding Metadata API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_meta.meta/api_meta/meta_api_intro.htm); [Deploying Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_deploying.htm))

During unlocked or 2GP version creation, the build system keeps only profile settings related to the package's metadata and discards the rest of the profile. Check Metadata Coverage for whether a type supports Metadata API, change sets, unlocked, or managed packaging. Org-dependent unlocked packages may depend on unpackaged metadata in the installation org.

mental_model.analogy: Shipping: change set = pallet between related docks; Metadata API deploy = crane loading XML; unlocked package = restockable labeled container; managed package = sealed AppExchange crate with a namespace lock. Git is the bill of lading. Passenger cargo is business data and uses a different terminal.
useful_mapping: change set → pallet, related orgs only
Metadata API / CLI deploy → crane for customization XML
unlocked package → internal container, VCS truth, subscriber-editable
managed 1GP → older crate; cannot migrate to 2GP today
Metadata Coverage → which cargo is allowed on which vessel
profile in a package version → only settings that relate to packaged metadata survive
where_it_breaks: Related-org change-set topology is not a real harbor map.
Org-dependent unlocked packages can lean on unpackaged metadata the crate does not contain.
Push upgrades exist for packages; pallets do not 'push.'
Coverage gaps mean some Setup cargo cannot board any of these vessels.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Change sets move metadata between related orgs. CLI/Metadata API deploys XML from Git. Unlocked packages are the usual internal versioned unit with VCS as truth. Managed 2GP is for AppExchange. You cannot migrate 1GP to 2GP today. None of these move Account rows.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with audience: AppExchange → 2GP. Internal versioning → unlocked. Related sandbox to prod and an admin-only team → change set may still fit, but I check Metadata Coverage and I know it is not Git. I mention profile trimming in package versions. I mention org-dependent unlocked when the org has unpackaged metadata the package needs. I never use a package install to migrate business data.

interview_questions.question: Unlocked package versus managed 2GP?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unlocked is the usual internal, source-driven, subscriber-editable container. Managed 2GP is for AppExchange distribution. Do not pick 2GP for a single enterprise unless you are actually distributing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote the unlocked guide's 'unless AppExchange' line and the 2GP guide's audience split. I mention VCS as truth for both modern types. I mention you cannot migrate 1GP to 2GP. I mention org-dependent unlocked when unpackaged org metadata is in play.
interview_questions.example: Internal LAB_ boarding → unlocked. Partner listing → 2GP.

interview_questions.question: Where do change sets still fit?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Related, connected orgs, often sandbox to production, for metadata an admin can select. They are not Git and not a data tool. Check Metadata Coverage.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I respect teams that still use them. I explain they will not reach an unrelated org, will not version like unlocked packages, and struggle with deletions compared with destructive manifests. If the team is already on CLI, I do not add change sets as a second source of truth.
interview_questions.example: Admin sends LAB_ validation rule from a developer sandbox to production via change set.
tradeoffs: Related-org only versus any authorized org

interview_questions.question: CIO wants one unlocked package on AppExchange next quarter. Response?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unlocked is not the AppExchange partner vehicle. Plan a managed 2GP. Unlocked stays for internal. You cannot migrate a 1GP later as a shortcut either.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate internal modularity from listing. Security review, manageability, and namespace are partner-process. I would not 'just namespace the unlocked package' as a listing strategy without reading current partner docs. I mark listing timelines as Needs verification with Partner.
interview_questions.example: Keep LabBoarding unlocked internally; start a 2GP if a true product listing is funded.
tradeoffs: Two code lines versus premature managed constraints
follow_ups: Can unlocked be a dependency of 2GP?

interview_questions.question: Package version installed but Admin profile looks unchanged. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unlocked/2GP version create keeps only profile settings related to the package metadata and discards the rest. Do not expect a full profile to ship.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I move authorization into permission sets in source (DEVOPS-008). I inspect what the version actually contained. I do not re-upload the entire Admin profile XML hoping it will stick. I still assign users separately from packaging.
interview_questions.example: Package grants LAB_ object CRUD via a permission set, not via a copied Admin profile.
follow_ups: What is a permission set group?
How do you grant to a scratch user?
weak_answer_warnings: The install failed because Admin did not match Git

interview_questions.question: When would you use org-dependent unlocked packages?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the package must depend on unpackaged metadata that already lives in the installation org, not when you can package the dependency cleanly.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat it as a debt marker. If the enterprise object cannot move, org-dependent may be honest. If we can package the dependency, I prefer modular unlocked packages. I still would not use this to sneak in business data.
interview_questions.example: Apex in an unlocked package references unpackaged Order on an enterprise org.
follow_ups: How do you test org-dependent in CI?
weak_answer_warnings: Org-dependent for AppExchange listings as the default

interview_questions.question: How is Metadata API deployment different from installing a package?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Metadata API/CLI deploy pushes unpackaged source (or a zip) into an org. Package install applies a versioned container. Both move metadata, not rows.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I can deploy force-app every commit in org development. I create versions when I need installable units, push upgrades, or AppExchange. Change sets are a third UI over metadata movement between related orgs. I pick using audience, topology, and coverage—not fashion.
interview_questions.example: PR CI: project deploy start to a scratch org. Release: package install 1.4.0 in UAT.
follow_ups: What is package upgrade vs deploy?
What is deprecated metadata in unlocked?

interview_questions.question: A type is in Git but never arrives via change set. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check Metadata Coverage for change sets. Check that the outbound set included dependencies. If the type is unsupported, use CLI or a manual step—do not keep adding it to the set.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Missing components are often coverage or forgotten children, not a 'Salesforce forgot Git.' If CLI can deploy it and change sets cannot, that is a channel gap. If neither can, it is unsupported metadata (DEVOPS-001/009).
interview_questions.example: A setup type with no change-set column in Coverage is added to a runbook instead of the outbound set.
tradeoffs: Switch channel versus redesign the feature
weak_answer_warnings: Git is wrong because the change set is empty

interview_questions.question: A Java lead says 'we'll just put it in Maven.' Translate to Salesforce packaging.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The closest internal analog is an unlocked package version from Git, not Maven Central. AppExchange is managed 2GP. Change sets are not artifacts. Metadata API deploy is more like rsync of XML.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map coordinates: sfdx-project.json packageDirectories, package version create, install. I warn about coverage, profile trimming, and 1GP. I keep business data out. I do not invent Maven-Salesforce federation.
interview_questions.example: LabBoarding 1.2.0 as the artifact CI installs in a scratch org, analogous to a versioned jar—but it is metadata, not bytecode-on-Maven.
tradeoffs: Familiar JVM mental model versus platform coverage
Public registry versus Dev Hub package records
